verses.text: In the beginning, God created the sky and the earth.
verses.strongs_text: In the beginning{H7225}, God{H430} created{H1254} the sky{H8064} and the earth{H776}.
notes: H430 'elohim' — singular verb 'bara' (Qal perfect 3ms) governs a morphologically plural noun. The ים- ending here functions as an intensifier ('the Mighty One,' 'the Fullness of God') rather than a numerical plural, as demonstrated by the singular verb throughout this chapter.
H8064 'shamayim' rendered 'sky' per word study finding: the physical sky/expanse above, from a root meaning 'to be lofty.' The ים- ending functions as intensifying rather than pluralizing.
H853 'et' (object marker) appears twice — untranslatable in English but marks 'the sky' and 'the earth' as definite direct objects.

verses.text: And the earth had become waste and emptiness, and darkness was over the face of the deep. And the spirit [or: wind, breath] of God was hovering over the face of the water.
verses.strongs_text: And the earth{H776} had become{H1961} waste{H8414} and emptiness{H922}, and darkness{H2822} was over{H5921} the face{H6440} of the deep{H8415}. And the spirit{H7307} [or: wind, breath] of God{H430} was hovering{H7363} over{H5921} the face{H6440} of the water{H4325}.
notes: H1961 'hayetah' — Qal perfect 3fs. Often rendered 'was,' but hayah is emphatic in Hebrew (not a mere copula). 'Had become' captures the completed-action force. Whether the earth was created in this state or became so is a long-standing interpretive question; the verb itself supports both readings.
H8414 'tohu' — desolation, wasteland, formlessness. Rendered 'waste' rather than 'without form' for directness.

H7307 'ruach' — the semantic range (spirit/wind/breath) is genuinely active here. The Piel participle 'merachephet' (hovering/brooding) suggests animate agency, favoring 'spirit,' but the physical image of wind over water is also present.
H7363 'merachephet' — Piel participle feminine singular, matching 'ruach.' Means 'hovering' or 'brooding' (as a bird over its nest, cf. Deut 32:11). Rendered 'hovering' rather than KJV 'moved.'
H4325 'mayim' — rendered 'water' (singular sense) per the principle that the ים- ending on this word is inherent to the noun, not a numerical plural.

verses.text: And God said, "Let there be an expanse in the midst of the water, and let it be separating between water and water."

verses.text: And God created the human in his image — in the image of God he created him. Male and female he created them.

The poetic structure is tripartite: (1) God created the human in his image, (2) in God's image he created him, (3) male and female he created them. The shift from singular 'him' to plural 'them' is present in the Hebrew.

verses.text: And God saw all that he had made, and look — it was exceedingly good. And there was evening and there was morning — the sixth day.
verses.strongs_text: And God{H430} saw{H7200} all{H3605} that{H834} he had made{H6213}, and look{H2009} — it was exceedingly{H3966} good{H2896}. And there was{H1961} evening{H6153} and there was{H1961} morning{H1242} — the sixth{H8345} day{H3117}.
notes: H3966 'me'od' — 'exceedingly, very.' From a root suggesting vehemence or intensity. Here it intensifies 'good' — not merely good, but forcefully, emphatically good.

Unlike days 1–5, 'the sixth day' (yom hashishi) has the definite article on the ordinal number. This is the only day in Genesis 1 where the ordinal is made definite with the article, possibly marking it as climactic.

chapter_notes: H430 'Elohim' consistently takes singular verbs throughout this chapter (bara, vayomer, vayar, vayavdel, vayiqra, vaya'as, vayitten, vayevarekh). This singular verb agreement demonstrates that the ים- suffix functions as an intensifier rather than a numerical plural. The sole exception is verse 26 ('na'aseh' — 'let us make'), where the verb shifts to 1st person plural. This anomaly is textually significant and preserved as-is.
The refrain 'and there was evening and there was morning' closes each day. Note: evening precedes morning, establishing the Hebrew day-cycle as beginning at dusk.

The verb 'bara' (H1254, to create) appears only at three points: verse 1 (sky and earth), verse 21 (sea creatures and living things), and verse 27 (humanity — three times). All other acts of making use 'asah' (H6213, to make/do). This distinction may be intentional, with 'bara' reserved for genuinely new categories of existence.

The pattern 'and God said...and it was so...and God saw that it was good' structures the entire chapter. Day two notably lacks 'and God saw that it was good,' while day three receives two such declarations, and day six climaxes with 'exceedingly good.'

H5315 'nephesh' — consistently rendered 'breath' or 'breathing thing' throughout this chapter rather than 'soul.' The word's primary meaning is concrete: the breathing life-force that animates creatures. The abstract/spiritual connotation that 'soul' carries in English is not present in the Hebrew of Genesis 1.
